primary_multi_analyte.desc: TC>=240 OR HDL<40/50 OR TG>=200 OR LDL>=160 (TG/LDL from fasting sub-sample; non-fasting evaluated on TC/HDL only)

sensitivity_tc_hdl_only.desc: TC>=240 OR HDL<40/50 (full-MEC-sample analytes only; WTMEC2YR-valid)

weights_note: NHANES total cholesterol and HDL are measured on the full MEC sample and carry WTMEC2YR (correct for the unweighted primary and the design-weighted derivation). Triglycerides and calculated LDL are available only in the overnight-fasting sub-sample (~48% of adults >=40 here), which carries a distinct fasting sub-sample weight. Mixing them means no single weight is exactly right for the multi-analyte variable; this is why the design-weighted derivation is labelled indicative. The TC+HDL-only definition removes the sub-sample mismatch entirely.
conclusion: Switching to the uniform full-sample TC+HDL definition moves external AUROC 0.7737->0.7732, apparent 0.7911->0.7913, slope 0.8723->0.8597, CITL -0.2131->-0.2740; the incremental dAUROC over age stays ~0.0031. Headline conclusions (age-dominated, external AUROC ~0.77, persistent over-prediction, negligible clinical-variable gain) are unchanged; the tighter definition slightly enlarges the over-prediction (lower dyslipidaemia prevalence 0.446->0.290).
